title: Strong induction and decidable least witnesses in Heyting arithmetic

based_on.title: Logic and Proof, §17.2 Variants of Induction (HTML version 3.18.4)

based_on.title: From Constructive Mathematics to Computable Analysis via the Realizability Interpretation (doctoral thesis)
based_on.pages: §1.3.2 printed p.25, HA definition only; elementary internal developments supplied locally

summary: Construct full strong induction from cumulative histories, search decidable predicates for a least witness, and locate the excluded-middle cost of an unrestricted least-number schema.
abstract: Strong induction lets an arithmetic proof use every smaller input while keeping its parameters fixed. In Heyting arithmetic, a cumulative history formula derives this rule from ordinary induction for every full native predicate. The least-witness construction here uses internal decisions for the predicate. We construct the finite search dichotomy and the least-witness proof, prove uniqueness, and show that an unrestricted least-number schema would yield each arithmetic instance of excluded middle.
